intended_object: The canonical R-linear projection from the completed tensor coalgebra ∏_{n≥0} M^{⊗n} onto its reduced part ∏_{n>0} M^{⊗n}, which drops the empty-word (degree-0) component. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the companion lemmas (ofCompleted_apply, ofCompleted_toCompleted).
explanation: `CompletedTensorWords R M` is `∀ n : ℕ, TensorPower R n M`, and `CompletedReducedTensorWords R M` is `∀ n : {n // 0 < n}, TensorPower R n.1 M`. The definition `LinearMap.pi fun n ↦ LinearMap.proj n.1` sends x to (n ↦ x n.1). So it keeps every positive-length component unchanged and forgets the degree-0 one, which is exactly the intended projection. The lemmas in the file show it behaves as expected: it is a left inverse of the zero-insertion map, and it recovers x whenever x 0 = 0. The setting is a commutative semiring R and an R-module M, the natural one for tensor powers, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no completed tensor coalgebra, so it has no dedicated counterpart either.
